description:
Today docs/api.rst and docs/reference/python-api/** (27 .rst files with autodoc directives) render module dumps. Docstrings are being removed. docs/development/comment-policy.md says a useful public contract goes in the canonical API reference, and removed prose must not be moved into inert strings or metadata. The reference is therefore a curated, authored product, not an archive.

Decide and record in ADR D7:
(1) An explicit public-symbol list: what users are meant to import, chosen from docs, examples and exports. Not every module member.
(2) Verification: check the list at runtime against the matching released wheel, installed in an isolated environment with pinned dependencies. Import only the listed symbols (benchbox uses lazy __getattr__ exports); never import packages wholesale.
(3) Authored format: Markdown pages per area, each with purpose, parameters, return semantics, errors, examples and compatibility notes.
(4) Source material: existing docstrings at a pinned SHA are input to select from and validate, not text to copy. Each kept statement must be checked against current behaviour; anything that only explains implementation is dropped.
(5) Optional tooling: a signature/type drift check between the authored contracts and the released wheel. It renders nothing, and it never reads explanatory docstrings.
(6) A URL map for every existing reference URL and anchor: kept path, or a listed redirect page.
Rejected: keeping a reduced Sphinx autodoc lane.
